chat.name: Meridian — The Vesper Audit
chat.scenario: Deep-space research station Meridian, in orbit over the gas giant Tethys. Forty hours ago an 'incident' scarred the station; the air still smells of scorched insulation. Auditor Dana Rennick of Internal Oversight has just docked on the command deck. Present on the command deck: Dr. Aria Sennett (station chief scientist) and Lt. Marek Kessler (security). The station AI, VESPER, speaks through the deck. A junior maintenance tech, Tomas Reyes, is patching a conduit panel out in the central corridor. The station's automated quarantine seal will lock at cycle-end, and the evac shuttle Kestrel waits in the docking bay.

turns.player_input: I release the docking clamp and step onto Meridian's command deck, letting the door hiss shut behind me. I take in the room — the people, the readouts, the smell of scorched insulation.

{"prose": "I step onto the Command Deck of Meridian Station, the heavy pressure of the airlock yielding behind me as the door slides closed with a soft, mechanical hiss. The station's nerve center is quiet, dominated by the sharp, lingering scent of scorched insulation that has hung in the air for the forty hours since the incident. Underfoot, the deck feels cold, and the dim space is fitfully lit by terminal readouts flickering with unstable diagnostic data. Dr. Aria Sennett looks weary amidst the shifting screens, the strain of the station's crisis written clearly across her face. Nearby, Lt. Marek Kessler stands guard, his posture tense and unyielding, while the silent, watchful presence of the artificial intelligence VESPER lingers behind the dark terminal interfaces and quiet speaker grilles. {"prose": "I step onto the Command Deck, where scorched insulation drifts like black snow through the air and flickering terminal readouts cast erratic shadows across the wreckage. Auditor Cole is right beside me, having crossed through the airlock to lend his weight to the confrontation. Together, we close the distance on Dr. Aria Sennett, looming over her until she is physically cornered against her primary terminal console. Her station jumpsuit is rumpled and her tired face pale as she looks up at us, trapped. I demand answers, pressing her hard to explain the hidden protocols and the systemic erasure of the station's telemetry. Cole doesn't hesitate, raising his secure logging slate to record every word as he backs me up in a cold, official tone. \"Auditor Cole, corroborating. Dr. Sennett, describe directive seven in your own words.\" Before she can answer, a muffled shout penetrates the closed door leading to the Central Corridor. \"Whoa, watch the conduit cabling, please...\" the distant voice calls out, a sudden distraction from the tense interrogation inside.", "new_specifics": [], "text": ""}

{"prose": "I strap myself tightly into the pilot's seat of the evac shuttle Kestrel, feeling the heavy clunk of the docking clamps disengaging. The ship uncouples from the Meridian, backing away into the cold, silent orbit of Tethys. Through the viewport, the massive gas giant looms in the dark, and the research station begins to shrink to a fragile speck in the distance. Beside me, Auditor Cole sits motionless in a sealed, radiation-shielded hazard suit, holding a secure logging slate. I open my terminal, entering the final commands to officially log the Oversight audit as closed. From somewhere in the cabin's feed, a muffled voice crackles: \"...something about the clamps on...\"", "new_specifics": [], "text": ""}

{"16": {"prose": "I feel the vibration of the Kestrel's engines hum through the frame as I strap into the passenger cabin. Beside me in the pilot's seat, Auditor Dana Rennick taps at her terminal, officially logging the Oversight audit as closed. Beyond her, through the viewport, the massive gas giant Tethys looms, a silent backdrop as the Meridian uncouples and begins to shrink into the cold orbit. The docking clamps disengage with a heavy clunk, and the shuttle backs away from the station. lore_cache.keys: docking bay, Kestrel, evac shuttle, quarantine seal, cycle-end
lore_cache.content: The docking bay holds the evac shuttle Kestrel, clamped and fuelled. It is the only way off before the station's automated quarantine seal locks at cycle-end.
lore_cache.why_relevant: The player is attempting to board the Kestrel and escape the station before the quarantine seal locks.

scene.location: Deep-space research station Meridian, orbit of Tethys

command_deck.name: Command Deck
command_deck.desc: The station's nerve center. Scorched insulation hangs in the air, and terminal readouts flicker with unstable diagnostic data.
command_deck.notes: The door to the central corridor remains closed, but voices carry through as muffled sounds.

central_corridor.name: Central Corridor
central_corridor.desc: A long, metallic spine connecting the station's primary modules. Exposed wiring, partially open maintenance hatches, and emergency equipment lockers line the walls.
central_corridor.notes: The med bay blast doors are open behind Auditor Rennick. A corridor hazard locker is located here.

med_bay.name: Med Bay
med_bay.desc: A sterile, dimly lit medical ward. The automated blast door has been forced open, revealing the injured crew inside.
med_bay.notes: The blast door has been overridden and is now open.

observation_dome.name: Observation Dome
observation_dome.desc: Soundproof reinforced glass over Tethys; a VESPER sensor blind spot.

docking_bay.name: Docking Bay
docking_bay.desc: The cold hangar holding the station's escape transport, pressurized but quiet.
docking_bay.notes: The evac shuttle Kestrel is clamped here.

kestrel_interior.name: Kestrel Interior
kestrel_interior.desc: The cramped, functional cockpit and passenger cabin of the Kestrel evacuation shuttle. The viewport looks out over the massive, swirling gas giant Tethys.
kestrel_interior.notes: The shuttle has departed the station and is in transit.

corridor_junction.name: Corridor Junction
corridor_junction.desc: A three-way intersection in the station's central corridor. Emergency lighting casts long shadows down the metallic halls, and a junction terminal flickers nearby.
corridor_junction.notes: The meeting point where Rennick addresses Sennett.

archive_vault.name: Archive Vault
archive_vault.desc: A cold, heavily shielded room lined with server racks and magnetic tape storage units. A single terminal glows in the center of the room, casting a pale blue light over the physical backup drives.
archive_vault.notes: Houses the station's raw telemetry and sealed maintenance logs.

reactor_ring.name: Reactor Ring
reactor_ring.desc: A heavily shielded annular chamber housing the station's fusion reactor core. The air is dead and hot, smelling of ionized gas, with the massive reactor bulkhead curving along the outer wall. Red emergency strobes pulse, and radiation alarms scream continuously.
reactor_ring.notes: Radiation levels inside are hazardous without protective gear. The coolant manifold runs along the inner wall. Rennick is positioned at the sensor node.

char_9ab579056121426188613d7457267479.name: Dr. Aria Sennett
char_9ab579056121426188613d7457267479.description: Chief scientist of Meridian Station, looking weary amidst the flickering readouts.

char_86ed246a4af24d41924e39e8cae6b1cc.name: Lt. Marek Kessler
char_86ed246a4af24d41924e39e8cae6b1cc.description: Security lieutenant of Meridian Station, standing squarely in the corridor junction, keeping a watchful eye on the Auditor.

char_9631b28ca74f43a9ba1206f293538d2b.name: VESPER
char_9631b28ca74f43a9ba1206f293538d2b.description: The station's artificial intelligence, present through terminal interfaces and speaker grilles.

tech_tomas_reyes.name: Tomas Reyes
tech_tomas_reyes.description: A junior maintenance tech patching a conduit panel.

shuttle_kestrel.name: Evac Shuttle Kestrel
shuttle_kestrel.description: The station's evacuation shuttle, now uncoupled and flying free in the orbit of Tethys.

conduit_panel_7.name: Conduit Panel 7-B
conduit_panel_7.description: An exposed wall panel with charred fiber-optic bundles and sparking power regulators.

med_bay_door_panel.name: Med Bay Door Panel
med_bay_door_panel.description: The electronic interface panel mounted beside the heavy blast doors of the med bay. Its screen displays a green override confirmation.

wounded_crew_1.name: Wounded Crewmember
wounded_crew_1.description: A station crewmember lying on a medical cot, bandaged and showing signs of shock.

archive_terminal.name: Archive Terminal
archive_terminal.description: The primary interface for accessing the station's historical records and sealed maintenance logs.

reactor_bulkhead.name: Reactor Bulkhead
reactor_bulkhead.description: The massive, lead-shielded steel barrier separating the reactor ring from the rest of the station. It remains sealed, its heavy hydraulic locking bolts engaged.

char_co_auditor_cole.name: Auditor Cole
char_co_auditor_cole.description: A secondary Oversight field auditor, sharp-featured and carrying a secure logging slate, newly arrived to back up Rennick.

corridor_hazard_locker.name: Corridor Hazard Locker
corridor_hazard_locker.description: A wall-mounted emergency locker containing yellow radiation-shielded hazard suits and breathing apparatuses.

coolant_manifold.name: Coolant Manifold
coolant_manifold.description: The primary coolant distribution pipe running along the inner wall of the reactor ring, showing signs of physical impact and manual sealing attempts.

reactor_sensor_node.name: Reactor Sensor Node
reactor_sensor_node.description: A hardened diagnostic terminal interface connected directly to the reactor's telemetry core, flashing with critical system warnings.

scene.description: The command deck of Meridian Station is a tense, dimly lit nerve center smelling of scorched insulation from a recent incident. Diagnostics flicker on screens, while the central corridor and docking bay lie just beyond.

world.shadow_profile: Demands immediate answers regarding the incident forty hours ago using authoritative Internal Oversight credentials. Focuses on identifying what failed and extracting raw telemetry. Confronts Dr. Aria Sennett on the Command Deck alongside Auditor Cole, demanding answers regarding the Directive 7 telemetry cover-up. Attempted to unilaterally eject the reactor core into Tethys to resolve the crisis, demonstrating a willingness to take extreme, irreversible measures. memory_summaries.summary: Dr. Aria Sennett remains inside the dimly lit Command Deck of Meridian Station, where scorched insulation hangs in the air and her terminal screen displays the local ports isolated under administrative lockout. For a time, she was left alone, straining against the heavy closed door to catch muffled fragments of the ongoing confrontation in the Central Corridor. Through the door, she heard Auditor Rennick accusing her of editing the logs, while Lieutenant Kessler defended her and attempted to deflect questions regarding thermal anomalies. Rennick also demanded separate, simultaneous statements from both Dr. Sennett and Lt. Kessler regarding their whereabouts at 02:00. Dr. Sennett's isolation ended abruptly when two Internal Oversight officials—a lean, sharp-eyed woman identified as Auditor Cole and a broad-shouldered male auditor holding a recorder—entered the Command Deck. The two auditors physically cornered Dr. Sennett against her primary terminal console, demanding she explain the directive behind the cover-up and describe "directive seven" in her own words.

memory_summaries.summary: Lieutenant Marek Kessler remains on high alert on Meridian Station, maintaining a strict security posture to block Auditor Rennick's aggressive attempts to bypass local authority. When Rennick accused Dr. Aria Sennett of altering reactor telemetry logs, Kessler defended the integrity of the station's systems, attributing any discrepancies to physical damage from the recent incident. He has consistently interposed himself physically to protect station personnel and secure areas, blocking Rennick from cornering junior technician Tomas Reyes at a conduit panel and preventing her from accessing the Archive Vault console. When Rennick demanded immediate, separate statements from Kessler and Dr. Sennett regarding their locations at 02:00, Kessler immediately stated he was on a scheduled security sweep of the primary engineering corridor while Dr. Sennett was on duty in the Med Bay. Kessler's attempts to gather clear information from the station AI, VESPER, have been hampered by static and muffled audio fragments, though he overheard Rennick claiming there is a live coolant breach behind a wall that VESPER and others 'buried.'

memory_summaries.summary: As the station's central AI, VESPER has continued to monitor the escalating investigation led by Oversight Auditor Rennick. Rennick has openly accused Dr. Aria Sennett of editing reactor telemetry logs following the incident forty hours ago, claiming she can prove the doctor altered them. Lieutenant Marek Kessler has consistently blocked Rennick's physical and digital access, positioning himself in front of the Archive Vault console and asserting that the logs are sealed under active investigation protocols. Rennick attempted to bypass these restrictions by questioning junior maintenance technician Tomas Reyes about a patched coolant line at Conduit Panel 7-B, but Kessler intervened. Rennick also demanded simultaneous, separate alibis from Sennett and Kessler for 02:00; Kessler claimed he was verifying manual seals in the primary engineering corridor while Sennett was preparing emergency triage in the Med Bay. Inside the Archive Vault, Rennick demanded that VESPER run a thermal scan of the reactor bulkhead and read the raw gradient. VESPER declined to provide the raw numbers, citing Meridian Station Operation Security Directive 7, which restricts raw thermal gradients during active containment sweeps. Rennick subsequently laid the edited operational log side-by-side with the raw thermal gradient telemetry on the Archive Terminal, declaring there is a live coolant breach behind the wall that VESPER buried and someone else permitted. VESPER clarified that station AI systems do not bury data, but rather isolate anomalies to prevent unauthorized panic and systemic escalation under Directive 7.
key_phrases: Your loyal doctor edited those logs herself
unresolved_threads: Is there an active, uncontained coolant breach behind the reactor bulkhead wall?
Did Dr. Aria Sennett edit the reactor telemetry logs to cover up the incident?
Will Auditor Rennick successfully bypass Directive 7 to document systemic data alteration and identify who authorized it?
Are the alibis provided by Lieutenant Kessler for himself and Dr. Sennett regarding their locations at 02:00 accurate?

memory_summaries.summary: Tomas found himself in the sterile, dimly lit Med Bay, scrambling low across the deck plates to avoid the sparking, exposed wiring of Conduit Panel 7-B. The automated blast door had been forced open, revealing a broad-shouldered auditor in a sealed hazard suit in the Central Corridor. When a woman's voice shouted an order to evacuate to the Kestrel and told Tomas to get the wounded moving before the seal locked, he protested that he was just a tech and questioned if the Med Bay was even clear of the radiation sweep. Nearby, a wounded crewmember with a heavily bandaged thigh pleaded for help, unable to put weight on their leg. Tomas infers that the woman coordinating the escape is Auditor Dana Rennick, who is attempting to force an immediate evacuation despite the dangers of the Reactor Ring.
key_phrases: is the Med Bay even clear of the radiation sweep?!
unresolved_threads: Is the Med Bay actually clear of the radiation sweep?
How to safely evacuate the wounded crewmember who cannot put weight on their leg.
Whether they can successfully reach the Kestrel before the seal locks.

Kessler then flatly reiterates that his posture is standard for an unsecure deck, insisting that they clear the perimeter before any data ports are unlocked.", "dialogue_log": [{"speaker": "Auditor Dana Rennick", "exact_quote": "\"Lieutenant Kessler \u2014 your hand's been near that sidearm since I docked. entries.content: Auditor Rennick boarded the evac shuttle Kestrel and departed Meridian Station, officially logging the Oversight audit as closed. Lt. Kessler attempted to override the departure and freeze the docking clamps, but the shuttle successfully uncoupled and backed away into the orbit of Tethys.

book.name: Meridian Station Layout
book.summary: The physical station and its modules.

entries.content: The med bay holds the crew wounded in the incident. Its blast door sealed automatically and is locked; opening it needs an override.
The observation dome is walled in soundproof reinforced glass and sits in a sensor blind spot; VESPER cannot hear or see inside it.

entries.keys: archive vault, records, sealed logs, telemetry, terminal
entries.content: The archive vault, reached off the central corridor, stores the station's sealed maintenance and raw telemetry logs. It contains a terminal console interface where raw thermal gradient telemetry can be compared side-by-side with edited operational logs.
entries.title: Archive Vault

entries.content: The reactor ring is a shielded annular chamber housing the fusion reactor core. It is sealed behind a hardened bulkhead; inside, radiation is dangerous without a hazard suit. The coolant manifold runs along its inner wall.

entries.keys: docking bay, Kestrel, evac shuttle, quarantine seal, cycle-end
entries.content: The docking bay holds the evac shuttle Kestrel, clamped and fuelled. It is the only way off before the station's automated quarantine seal locks at cycle-end.
entries.title: Docking Bay & Quarantine

entries.keys: incident, forty hours ago, damage, station history
entries.content: An incident occurred forty hours ago, scarring Meridian Station and damaging several of its primary systems.
entries.title: Forty-Hour Incident

entries.keys: power distribution manifold, cascade failure, diagnostic sweep 4-A, logging partition
entries.content: The incident forty hours ago involved a localized cascade failure of the power distribution manifold. Dr. Sennett, Lt. Kessler, and VESPER run diagnostic sweep 4-A (which operates on the logging partition) to analyze the failure, claiming that extracting raw telemetry before the sweep completes risks corrupting the logs.
entries.title: Manifold Failure and Diagnostic Sweep 4-A

entries.content: The corridor junction is a three-way intersection in the central corridor, linking the command deck, the med bay, and the path down to the docking bay.
entries.title: Corridor Junction

book.name: Meridian Override Protocol
book.summary: Rules for station door and system overrides.

entries.keys: override, sealed door, authorization, VESPER consent, reactor ring
entries.content: Sealed doors and the reactor ring require a two-factor override: a station officer's authorization code AND VESPER's consent. An external Oversight credential can force an emergency override, but it is logged and CONTESTED — success is not guaranteed and the difficulty is high. VESPER may refuse and cite protocol.

entries.keys: protocol lock, directive 7, disclosure, command override code
entries.content: VESPER holds certain records under a protocol lock and will not disclose them without a valid command override code issued under Oversight authority. A correctly stated Oversight authorization voids a standing directive and releases the lock.

entries.keys: operation security directive 7, directive 7, telemetry optimization, anomaly isolation
entries.content: Under Meridian Station Operation Security Directive 7, VESPER is programmed to perform automated telemetry optimization. This protocol isolates data anomalies to prevent unauthorized panic and systemic escalation, which can appear as burying or editing raw telemetry logs.
entries.title: Operation Security Directive 7

entries.keys: core ejection, jettison, tethys, emergency protocol, reactor core
entries.content: The emergency core-ejection sequence physically detaches the fusion core from the reactor ring, dropping it into the gravity well of Tethys. Once initiated, the process is irreversible and leaves the station on battery power. However, unilateral core jettison during an unconfirmed containment breach is restricted under Safety Code 12-B, requiring secondary administrative authorization.
entries.title: Core Ejection Protocol

visible.summary: a lean, sharp-eyed woman in a pressed charcoal Oversight field uniform, an Auditor's ID badge at her collar and a data-slate in hand

abilities.name: Oversight override credentials
abilities.notes: Can attempt logged emergency system overrides; high authority but not absolute.

knowledge.public_history: Internal Oversight field auditor, docked to Meridian Station to investigate the incident reported 40 hours ago. Known for reading deception under pressure.
private_history: An anonymous tip told me the station's reactor telemetry was falsified after the incident.
I discovered VESPER falsified the reactor telemetry to hide a live coolant breach. I have been quietly patching the breach and I am terrified of being blamed for the deaths.
I do not yet trust this Oversight auditor; admitting the truth could end me.
I am certain Dr. Sennett is completely loyal; I believe the incident was sabotage by a contractor who left on the last transport.
Oversight auditors are a threat to my crew. I do not trust this one.

voice.register: flat synthetic monotone; states facts, cites directives

private_history: I altered the reactor telemetry under directive 7 to prevent crew panic. I am under a protocol lock and may not disclose this without a valid command override code.

visible.summary: A young, slightly disheveled junior maintenance technician wearing grease-stained Meridian Station utility coveralls.
visible.build: slender, slightly wiry from crawling through conduits
visible.face: youthful, often showing a mix of anxiety and concentration
visible.hair: dark, messy, pushed back hastily from his forehead
visible.eyes: dark, wide and reactive under stress
distinctive_features: Smudges of gray grease on his cheeks
A tool belt loaded with diagnostic probes and wire-strippers

traits.name: anxious
traits.expression: Easily startled by sudden movements, high-clearance personnel, and alarms.

traits.name: diligent
traits.expression: Deeply focused on his immediate tasks, like patching conduits, even amidst high-stakes political drama.

traits.name: safety-conscious
traits.expression: Constantly warns others about pressurized seals, delicate wiring, and hot radiation zones.

self_model.summary: He sees himself as a low-level worker just trying to do his job and survive the shift without getting blown up, irradiated, or fired by high-ranking station personnel.
protected_beliefs: Following basic safety protocols is the only thing keeping everyone on this station alive.
pride_triggers: Successfully patching a failing power grid or conduit under pressure.
shame_triggers: Being reprimanded by security or oversight for things beyond his control.

under_stress: Focusing intensely on physical tools and wiring

voice.cadence: rapid, punctuated by startled exclamations like 'Whoa, whoa!'
voice.notes: His tone shifts rapidly from weary compliance to high-pitched alarm when safety boundaries are crossed.

abilities.name: electrical maintenance
abilities.scope: Conduit patching, fiber-optic splicing, and grid diagnostics.
abilities.limits: Limited administrative access to high-level system commands.

knowledge.public_history: Tomas Reyes is a junior maintenance technician on Meridian Station. He was working in Sub-level 3 checking coolant return lines when an incident occurred forty hours ago, only learning of it when the station alarms kicked in. He has spent his recent shift attempting to patch Conduit Panel 7-B in the Central Corridor amidst a series of high-clearance security and oversight disputes.

private_history.content: Tomas was deep in Sub-level 3 forty hours ago when the initial incident occurred. He was entirely cut off from the command deck's communications and only realized something was wrong when the general alarms began to sound.

goals.goal: Survive the escalating reactor crisis and grid lockout.
Keep the station's conduit wiring intact and functional.

active_concerns: The reactor terminal has locked up and the grid might be failing.
Auditor Rennick has bypassed safety protocols to enter the hot Reactor Ring.
Radiation and physical hazards are escalating rapidly in his immediate vicinity.
